samples.summary: The frontend's duplicate nesting cap (`treeNodeToBlock` in `yorkie-doc-store.ts`) has no test at all
samples.evidence: The diff adds the identical depth cap twice: once in `packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts` (covered by the new `packages/docs/test/model/table-nesting.test.ts`) and once in the frontend's live twin `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts` (`treeNodeToBlock(node, depth = 0)`, depth threaded through `treeNodeToRow`/`treeNodeToCell`, and the two `map((c) => treeNodeToBlock(c))` wrappers in `treeToDocument` that stop `map`'s index arg being read as depth). The frontend is the actual production read path for collaborative docs. Grepping the frontend for `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` / `treeNodeToBlock` matches only the source file — no test in `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts` (or elsewhere) builds a nested-table tree or asserts truncation, and no test pins the `map` wrapper (a regression back to `.map(treeNodeToBlock)` would silently pass the array index as depth and truncate header/footer tables from index 32 onward, with nothing failing). Since the frontend has no `tsc` lane either, this duplicated guard can rot undetected.

samples.summary: The layout cap is tested only with `not.toThrow()`; the line/`blockBoundaries` correspondence the cap's comment calls load-bearing is unasserted
samples.evidence: `layoutCellBlocks` pushes exactly one placeholder line past the cap, and its comment in `table-layout.ts` says "keeps the cell's line/`blockBoundaries` arrays in step with its blocks — every caret and hit-test index depends on that correspondence". The only layout test (`lays out a chain deep enough to overflow the stack`) asserts `expect(() => computeTableLayout(...)).not.toThrow()` and nothing else, so a truncation that pushed zero or two lines — desynchronising `blockBoundaries` and thus mis-placing every caret/hit-test in that cell — would still pass. No other test covers a past-cap layout (grep for `blockBoundaries` in `test/view/nested-table-layout.test.ts` finds none).

samples.summary: The new `buildCellRangeRects` index clamp is not exercised by any test
samples.evidence: The diff adds `rowStart/rowEnd/colStart/colEnd` clamps in `buildCellRangeRects` bounded by `tl.cells.length` / `tl.columnXOffsets.length`, justified as a backstop for a rectangle that 'slipped past' `normalizeCellRange` (a table that resolves in the layout but not in normalization). The only clamp test — `clamps a peer-written cell rectangle to the table it names` in `nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:389` — goes through `normalizeCellRange` with a resolvable table, so the values reaching `buildCellRangeRects` are already in range. Removing the new clamp would not fail any test.

samples.summary: The new cycle guards in `findOuterCellAddress` and `findOutermostTableId` have no test
samples.evidence: `resolveNestedTableLayout`, `normalizeRange`, `resolvePositionPixel` and `Doc.findBlock` each got a cyclic-`blockParentMap` test in `nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:307-422`, but the two new `seen`-set guards added to `TextEditor.findOuterCellAddress` and the new `TextEditor.findOutermostTableId` are covered by none: grepping `packages/docs/test` for `findOuterCellAddress|findOutermostTableId|resolveCellGesture` returns no matches. These are private, so a test would need to drive them through a pointer gesture with a cyclic map; absent that, a regression re-introducing the unbounded `while (true)` on the pointer path would ship green.

samples.summary: 'shift+click across the merged row covers the merge whole' asserts only a rectangle count, not which cells are painted
samples.evidence: `expect(rects).toHaveLength(5)` is the whole assertion. Five selection-coloured fills would also result from a wrong rectangle (e.g. the wrong two columns, or rows 0–2 of a different column pairing), so the test cannot distinguish 'the merge is covered whole' — the behaviour its name claims — from several incorrect paints. The sibling file `table-drag-merge-selection.test.ts` shows the stronger read-back (`cellsOf()` mapping fills to `row,col` addresses against a calibrated grid); this nested file has no equivalent and only sorts raw rects.

samples.summary: `clampCellIndex`'s unresolved-table path (max = Infinity) and non-finite `end` are untested
samples.evidence: `normalizeCellRange` is only tested with a resolvable 2×2 table (`nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:389`), which exercises finite `maxRow`/`maxCol`. The branch where `table` is undefined (`maxRow = maxCol = Infinity`, so `Math.min(trunc(raw), Infinity)` must leave large values alone and `Math.max(Infinity, 0)` is used as a bound) has no test, nor does a non-finite `end` index (only `start.colIndex` is `NaN` in the existing case). Both are the peer-written-input paths the change exists to harden.

verdict.reason: The frontend defines its own copy of the nesting cap: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:466-484 implements `treeNodeToBlock(node, depth = 0)` with `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` truncation, threaded through treeNodeToRow (436) / treeNodeToCell (445), and treeToDocument (548-568) wraps three call sites as `.map((c) => treeNodeToBlock(c))` specifically so map's index is not read as depth. This code is on the live read path (getDocument -> treeToDocument at line 814). The only test of this logic anywhere is packages/docs/test/model/table-nesting.test.ts, which imports `../../src/model/crdt-tree.js` — the engine copy, not the frontend's. I searched beyond the reviewer's paths: glob **/*nesting* (docs package only), repo-wide grep for treeNodeToBlock/treeToDocument/MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH (no frontend test hits), frontend tests for nested/deep/RangeError/large depths (all unrelated: nested batches, nested cell attrs, single-level nested tables e.g. yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2916-2926), a docs analogue of tests/app/slides/yorkie-slides-equivalence.test.ts (none exists), and any source-parity/duplication guard reading yorkie-doc-store.ts (scripts/verify-entropy.mjs:46 and scripts/test/verify-entropy.test.mjs:80 are doc-link prose handling, not a parity check). No counterexample found: no test builds a >cap nested-table tree against the frontend reader, and nothing pins the map wrapper (existing nested-table tests nest one level, far below the cap, so a regression to `.map(treeNodeToBlock)` would pass silently). Failure of this guard means a peer-writable deep nesting chain overflows the stack on read and the document cannot be opened — user-visible, so major.

finding.summary: The second changed branch of `getSelectedText` (cell-internal selection inside a *nested* table) has no test asserting the plain-text flavour
finding.evidence: This delta makes two nested-aware fixes in `getSelectedText`: the `tableCellRange` branch and the cell-internal branch (`startCellInfo`/`endCellInfo`, ~line 806, comment "an ordinary text selection inside a *nested* table's cell copied as ''"). Only the first gets a new assertion (nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:250). For the cell-internal branch I found no test that checks `text/plain`: the closest existing test, copy-integrity.test.ts:354 'resolves a cell inside a nested table', selects `nc1` inside an inner table but asserts only `payloadBlocks(...)` (the WAFFLEDOCS_MIME flavour) — it would stay green with `getSelectedText` reverted to the flat `layout.blocks.find`. Impact if the fix regresses: copy from a nested table cell writes an empty `text/plain` to every external app, and the cut path (text-editor.ts:1482/1492 also call `getSelectedText`) deletes the text while putting nothing on the clipboard — silent data loss. A one-line `expect(written.get('text/plain')).toBe('Deep￼')` in copy-integrity.test.ts:354 would close it.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing coverage exists in the same new test file the reviewer says they read in full. nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:271-286 ('copying a text selection inside a nested cell writes that text') sets a plain caret range (offsets 0-4) on the paragraph block inside nested-table cell (2,1), dispatches a real `copy` event via copyFlavours(), and asserts `written.get('text/plain')` === 'r2c1'. A second test at :288-297 asserts a partial slice ('0c' from 'r0c1', offsets 1-3). Both target the cell-internal branch (their comment names it: "The *other* nested-aware lookup in getSelectedText ... takes the cell-internal branch rather than the cell-rectangle one"). Non-vacuity checked against selection.ts:856-878: once startCellInfo/endCellInfo resolve, the branch returns early, so reverting to the flat `layout.blocks.find(...)` lookup leaves tableData undefined for a nested table and returns '' at line 866 — both assertions would fail. The fixture gives each addressable inner cell distinct text (test:126-128), so a wrong cell also cannot pass. Wiring confirmed at text-editor.ts:1446 (copy) and :1492 (cut), which write text/plain from selection.getSelectedText, and the test drives the real copy event on the editor textarea rather than calling the method directly.
